claims.text: Adding a minor dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles to the refractory high-entropy alloy will improve high-temperature creep resistance.
The oxide addition will leave overall density nearly unchanged.
The oxide addition will leave room-temperature mechanical performance nearly unchanged.
The selected baseline is an equiatomic Mo-Nb-Ta-W refractory high-entropy alloy without dispersed second-phase particles.
The intervention is addition of 0.5-1 wt% Y2O3 through an oxide-dispersion-strengthening powder-processing and consolidation route.
The introduced Y2O3 nanoparticles will be stable at the stated high-temperature test condition.
The ODS route will produce a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin dislocations and grain boundaries.
The nanoscale oxides will inhibit dislocation motion at high temperature.
The nanoscale oxides will inhibit grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
Inhibition of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will increase creep rupture strength or rupture life.
Inhibition of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will reduce the steady-state creep strain rate.
The low oxide fraction will minimize adverse effects on room-temperature ductility.
The proposed creep benefit is expected to hold at approximately 1100 degrees Celsius under sustained load.
The creep benefit will occur only within a narrow oxide-addition range.
Excess oxide addition or oxide agglomeration may embrittle the alloy, especially at room temperature.
Excess oxide addition may cause appreciable density changes.
